newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rules out support for Africa coffee move.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rules out support for Africa coffee move.

text.p: Indonesia, the world's third largest coffee producer, said on Thursday it would not back an African initiative to cut-back output next year in an effort to bolster prices.

"If we restrain our supplies, there are free riders in the region who will take over our market (share)," Paian Nainggolan, Indonesia's government representative to the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), told Reuters.
"The free riders produce the same type and quality of coffee as we do," he said, adding the people behind the initiative so far had not formally sought Indonesia's support.

Nainggolan did not want to identify the "free riders," but Indonesia's main competitor in the region is Vietnam, which is not an ACPC member and therefore not bound to participate in the proposed scheme.
The Inter-African Coffee Organisation (IACO) agreed at a meeting in Abidjan in November to approach ACPC members with a scheme to lift prices by reducing roaster stocks.
The IACO said a ministerial committee comprising Ivory Coast, Uganda and Angola would hold "high level political and diplomatic consultations" with other ACPC members.
